subject: Co-build: Codemeld lightweight SDK + tracing onboarding
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha@codemeld.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@codemeld.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 17:12:00 +0000
Subject: Integration proposal — Codemeld lightweight SDK + Redwood tracing

Hi Vanessa,

Hope you’re well — I’m Asha, Head of Partnerships at Codemeld. We build a developer-focused prompt tooling and orchestration SDK (LangChain-compatible subset) that surfaces prompt templates, evaluation hooks, and a lightweight tracing shim that can emit spans to third-party tracing endpoints. A few customers have asked for a Redwood-native pathway to run models through your Dedicated/private offerings while preserving our prompt telemetry and attribution.

High-level ask: evaluate a short co-build to ensure our SDK can be used as a first-class integration with Redwood’s tracing and telemetry surface (prefix caching hints, token attribution, model routing metadata). We’d like to validate in a small pilot:
- SDK runtime adapter (LangChain-compatible client)
- Trace export to Redwood’s tracing endpoint (or an agreed proxy)
- Preflight security/compliance checklist and minimal SOW for a 6-week pilot

Attached: codemeld-sdk-arch-diagram.png (visual), initial answers to our security questionnaire (security-compliance-answers.xlsx). I can also share a one-page SOW draft if useful.

Would love to schedule a technical sync next week with your runtime/product and partnerships leads. Proposed attendees from our side: me + Tom (engineer) + one of our infra folks.

Thanks —
Asha Rao
Head of Partnerships, Codemeld Inc
attachments: codemeld-sdk-arch-diagram.png, security-compliance-answers.xlsx
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@codemeld.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Integration proposal — Codemeld lightweight SDK + Redwood tracing

Hi Asha — great to meet you over email, thank you for the overview and the attachments. Happy to run a pilot; this aligns with our ISV partner program goals.

Quick notes up front so we can make the sync productive:
- Goals: validate trace semantics (token-level attribution + prompt metadata), confirm host/runtime compatibility for Dedicated/private, and agree an acceptance checklist for the pilot.
- Technical owners: I’ve looped in Marissa (ISV partner engineering lead) and Karthik (runtime/telemetry).
- Pre-read: can you provide a short example repo or minimal demo that shows the SDK runtime integrated with a LangChain flow (preferably a small Dockerfile + run instructions)? That will let our infra team run a local smoke test before the call.
- Telemetry expectations: we prefer a lightweight export that includes model_id, sequence_id, prompt_hash, and token attribution offsets. If you can surface those fields as labels on spans, it will speed acceptance.

Proposed times for a 60-minute technical sync (PST):
- Tue Dec 1, 10:00–11:00
- Tue Dec 1, 14:00–15:00
Please let us know which works and we’ll send a calendar invite.

For procurement/legal: we typically pilot under a small SOW with mutual NDA + limited data processing terms; if you can share a SOW draft ahead of the call we’ll circulate it through Licensing.

Thanks — looking forward to pairing on this.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Partner Integrations | Redwood Inference
attachments: none
From: Asha Rao <asha@codemeld.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@codemeld.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 11:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Integration proposal — Codemeld lightweight SDK + Redwood tracing

Vanessa — thanks for the quick reply and the helpful checklist. We attached a short demo repo link in the Drive folder and an initial SOW draft (integration-sow-draft.pdf) to this thread. Quick pointers to what we included:
- Demo: dockerized example showing LangChain-ish flow + our SDK emitting OTLP-compatible traces to a collector; README has run steps.
- Tracing: we currently send spans with these attributes: model.name, prompt.hash, session.id, token.start, token.end. We can add model_id and sequence_id labels if you prefer.
- Data handling: pilot mode defaults to ephemeral/local storage; we’ve flagged retention settings in the questionnaire.

We can do Tue Dec 1 at 14:00 PST — sending a calendar hold now. Attendees from Codemeld: me, Tom (backend), Priya (security engineer - tentatively).

Looking forward to the sync. Let us know if you want us to prepare a 10–15 minute live demo or keep it purely technical Q&A.

Best,
Asha

Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Integration proposal — Codemeld lightweight SDK + Redwood tracing (post-sync notes)

Fwd: Notes from today’s sync with Codemeld — quick internal summary and next steps.

Summary (15-min sync):
- Codemeld demo shows OTLP-compatible spans; their token.* attributes align closely with what we need but they do not yet emit Redwood-specific model_id and sequence_id labels.
- Actionable gaps:
  1) Label parity: Codemeld will add model_id and sequence_id to spans (target: this week).
  2) Sample app: Codemeld shared a dockerized example; infra will run a smoke test in our sandbox.
  3) SOW/legal: they shared integration-sow-draft.pdf; Licensing wants a short clause on telemetry ownership and retention during pilot.
  4) Security: Priya (Codemeld) confirmed ephemeral retention by default; we requested an attestation note (we have the spreadsheet).

Internal owners & deadlines:
- Runtime smoke test: Karthik to run by 12/03 and report failures (owner: karthik_iyer).
- Telemetry label add: Codemeld to confirm by 12/02 (owner: Asha/Tom).
- SOW revisions: Vanessa to coordinate with Licensing and send redlines by 12/04 (owner: vanessa_ortiz).

I’ll open a short checklist ticket in our partner board and attach the SOW and the security spreadsheet.

Marissa Cole
ISV Partner Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference
